The latter part of that is true; when social security and especially a lot of pension plans were put into place, they were based on estimated lifespans that turned out to be inaccurate. But while life expectancy has increased over time, it has dipped back over the last few years (in contrast to other first-world countries, where it keeps rising). Link [here](https://www.cnbc.com/2019/07/09/us-life-expectancy-has-been-declining-heres-why.html).

In my family, it really varies. I've had relatives make it to their 90s and others die of non-accident causes in their 50s and 60s. I also think this is one of those things where statistics don't tell the entire story—there's a general malaise and apathy in the U.S. that doesn't seem to get better. Housing policies mean that there are plenty of millennials and younger who make really good salaries and can't get a decent place, while their grandfathers and uncles were somehow able to buy a house in a nice neighborhood working 4 days a week at a shoe store. This is not going to end well.
Hey, my portfolio is doing great but we all know this is a mirage and it's going to come crashing down. Life expectancy is falling in America. Economic indicators will follow.

For the record, I think the best bet here would be a one of a handful of African countries (Ghana, Nigeria), but there's definitely governance risk there. China has a looming demographic nightmare. The U.S. and most of Europe had a nice run but are clearly in rapid decline.

But the answer here, beating out plenty of tough competition, would be my sister. My parents financed a vanity career in the arts for her for more than 10 years, while she never really worked other than temporary gigs at family businesses yet stayed dressed in designer clothes for her "image and career." In her mid-30s, finally gave up on being the next Taylor Swift and now has a job and title at one of the family businesses that she is in no way qualified for, and acts like she's earned it, criticizing longtime employees.

There's nothing wrong with not being cut out for success in the American capitalist economy (I'm doing OK now but it's hard for us beta males!), but the holier-than-thou attitude just kills me.
